clue.text: Pudding and wallop for the baseball player

definitions.meaning: a ... pudding is a baked pudding made from flour, egg and milk
to wallop is to strike repeatedly, to pound
the player at the plate swinging the bat

explanation.surface: A dessert and a hearty whack offered to someone on the diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions run together: the pudding (as in Yorkshire pudding mixture), the verb to beat, and the hitter in baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: Each sense is a dictionary meaning: a baked flour-and-egg mixture, to pound hard, and the hitter facing the pitcher.

clue.text: Same bonny tangle ? Not at all

indicators.note: a tangle is a muddle, so the letters of the two words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about a knot of hair, firmly denied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangle' shuffles the nine letters of SAME and BONNY.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic phrase of denial, meaning in no way whatever.

clue.text: Pre-eminent single state is up-to date

parts.note: pre-eminent means top, foremost
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A claim that a leading unitary nation is modern.
explanation.walkthrough: CAL is a standard short form of California.
explanation.definitionFit: Something topical deals with current affairs, so it is current and modern.

clue.text: Points on instruction for getting on line..:

parts.note: E for east, a compass point
N for north, another compass point
training is instruction or teaching

explanation.surface: Tips on teaching for falling into line, leading on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: One word 'Points' gives two compass points, E and N. 'on line' is a railway line: to entrain is to board a train; the ellipsis carries the sense on to 5 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Boarding a train, as troops do when moved by rail.

clue.text: Miners mistakenly rouse many

parts.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, the British miners' union

indicators.note: done mistakenly, the word rouse gets its letters in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Coal workers wrongly stir up a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miners' is the National Union of Mineworkers, Britain's coal miners' trade union; 'mistakenly' scrambles the word that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerous is a synonym for plentiful, existing in large number.

clue.text: such raw recruits, having to walk ?

definitions.text: such raw recruits, having to walk ?

parts.words: such raw recruits, having to walk ?
parts.note: raw recruits lack drilling; read as ..., a soldier with no train to board must march on foot

explanation.surface: Green soldiers forced to go on foot, carried on from 3 Down.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 3 Down: soldiers not put on a train must walk, and raw recruits are also unschooled.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw recruits are inexperienced, not yet drilled or schooled.

clue.text: Pitcher decapitates one of Joshua's woodmen

indicators.note: to decapitate is to cut off the head, so the woodman loses his first letter

parts.note: in the Book of Joshua the Gibeonites became hewers of wood and drawers of water

explanation.surface: A jug beheading a biblical woodcutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitates' removes the H from HEWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitcher is a large jug with a wide mouth, used for water.

clue.text: A very small prophet

parts.note: one of the Minor Prophets whose book, a single chapter, is the shortest in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A tiny seer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very small' is about the book, not the man: his is the shortest book of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Obadiah is one of the twelve Minor Prophets, and his book has only twenty-one verses.

clue.text: Ecclesiastical passage in Thorndike's book

definitions.meaning: a covered walkway between a cathedral's transept and chapter house
a 1927 novel by Russell Thorndike set in a cathedral

explanation.surface: A church scene described in a novelist's work.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a quoted extract from a book; 'passage' is a corridor, and the book is Russell Thorndike's mystery novel of that title.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a narrow covered way in a church precinct, and was also the title of Thorndike's novel.

clue.text: Bar security

definitions.meaning: a crosspiece, such as a bar separating horses in a stable or one on a cricket stump
money pledged to release an accused person until trial

explanation.surface: Protection at a pub or courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a crossbar and the sum deposited to free a prisoner pending trial.

clue.text: Oil found by wild Pathan outside Himalayan capital

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit outside, around, the next piece
wild means unruly, so the word Pathan has its letters thrown about
a capital is the first letter of the word Himalayan

explanation.surface: Petroleum discovered by a fierce tribesman beyond a mountain city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges PATHAN to NAPTHA; 'outside' puts it around H, the 'capital' of Himalayan. A Pathan is a Pashtun of Afghanistan and Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: A volatile flammable liquid distilled from petroleum or coal tar.

clue.text: They include punishment in this treatment

indicators.note: to include is to hold within, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a rap is a blow or rebuke, as in a rap on the knuckles

explanation.surface: A remark that a course of care involves penalties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'include' has the first word of the clue swallow the synonym for punishment; 'in this' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is remedial care given for illness or distress.

clue.text: Daisy may be out at this time

definitions.text: Daisy may be out at this time

parts.words: Daisy may be out at this time
parts.note: the purple aster named after a late-September feast flowers around that feast

explanation.surface: A woman called Daisy is not at home just now.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy looks like a woman's name and 'out' like away from home; the daisy is the flower and 'out' means in bloom, on the feast of St Michael, 29 September.
explanation.definitionFit: The Feast of St Michael on 29 September gives its name to the aster that blooms then.

clue.text: Captive bird ?

annotationWithheld.why: Captive bird ? (4): no parse found linking 'Captive bird' to RITE

clue.text: Record ten ton order causes dissatisfaction

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: put in a new order, the letters of ten and ton are rearranged

explanation.surface: Logging heavy weights brings grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' scrambles the six letters of 'ten ton'; 'causes' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Discontent is unhappiness with one's lot, a lack of contentment.

clue.text: Fast woman suffers a loss of capital

indicators.note: to suffer a loss is to lose something, here a letter
loss of a letter means taking that letter out of the name

parts.note: Atalanta, the swift huntress of Greek myth who outran her suitors

explanation.surface: A promiscuous woman loses money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast woman' suggests loose morals, but she is the runner Atalanta; she loses one A. The capital is that of the US state of Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlanta is the capital city of the state of Georgia.

clue.text: An orange car could be a sign of such presumption

indicators.note: the words could be rearranged into something else, so their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Driving a flashy coloured car as a show of self-importance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges the nine letters of AN ORANGE CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogance is overbearing presumption, an inflated sense of one's own importance.

clue.text: Also not one to enter lower down

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the single letter goes into the word

parts.note: nether means lower, as in the nether regions
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to go downstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts I inside NETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Used after a negative, as in 'nor I', it means likewise not.

clue.text: Treatments for those remaining French priests

parts.note: the rest are the others, those left over
curé is French for a parish priest

explanation.surface: Remedies for the surviving clergy in France.
explanation.walkthrough: CURES is the plural of French curé, a parish priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest cure is a medical regime of bed rest and quiet.

clue.text: Flayer of his horse ?

definitions.meaning: one who strips hides from animals
... Horse is an Indian cavalry regiment raised by James ...

explanation.surface: A man who strips the hide from his own mount.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone flaying his horse; the second sense is the founder of a regiment of horse, the cavalry unit that bears his name.
explanation.definitionFit: One who flays hides is a hide-stripper, and James of that name founded an Indian cavalry regiment.

clue.text: No fraction, for example, in between .

indicators.note: one piece goes in another, so it sits inside it

parts.note: inter- is the Latin prefix for between

explanation.surface: A whole number, perhaps, lying between others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the abbreviation inside the Latin prefix for between, as in international.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number, one with no fractional part.

clue.text: Writer's euphemism for the Devil

definitions.meaning: as in 'what the ...?', a polite stand-in for Satan

explanation.surface: An author's mild oath.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles of that name wrote Oliver Twist, and 'the dickens' softens 'the devil' in exclamations.

clue.text: Apostate in the red is liable to go astray

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other, so it sits inside it

parts.note: Eric the Red, the Norse explorer of Greenland
a rat is one who deserts a cause or party

explanation.surface: A turncoat in debt is likely to stray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the red' looks like being in debt, but 'the red' is the Norse explorer Eric the Red, and 'in' puts the turncoat inside his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means wandering, irregular, unpredictable in course.

clue.text: Carry to the' extremities to provide better facilities

indicators.note: the extremities of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Lugging gear to the far ends to improve amenities for gamblers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremities' takes T and E, the first and last letters of 'the'. The tail of the clue is a second hint: the tote is the totalisator, the betting machine that serves those who bet.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to lug or haul a load.

clue.text: " Here - -s bloom as they are told" (Brooke)

definitions.text: " Here - -s bloom as they are told" (Brooke)

parts.words: " Here - -s bloom as they are told" (Brooke)
parts.note: a line from Rupert Brooke's poem Grantchester, contrasting orderly German flower beds with English ones, with the flower missing

explanation.surface: A quotation with a gap from a poem by Rupert Brooke.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Old Vicarage, Grantchester, Brooke writes from Berlin that 'Here tulips bloom as they are told'; the blank takes the flower plus the printed S.
explanation.definitionFit: The line from Grantchester names the spring bulb flower whose plural fills the gap.

clue.text: Hardly altruistic, putting number one in the middle

parts.note: number one is oneself, the self or ego
centric means placed at the centre

explanation.surface: Selfishly putting oneself first and central.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number one' is slang for oneself, which fits the ego.
explanation.definitionFit: Egocentric means self-centred, the opposite of selflessly altruistic.

clue.text: Where curving branches meet in a focus point

indicators.note: the letters sit in the words focus point, running across the join

explanation.surface: A geometry note about curves meeting at a focal point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the letters lie inside 'focus point', across the gap between the words.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry, a cusp is the pointed spot where two arcs of a curve touch.

clue.text: Girl is to rise above, her, regrets ?

indicators.note: in a down entry the turned piece sits above, before, the other
in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the word is turned round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman resolves to overcome her disappointments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is to rise' looks like resolve; 'to rise' turns TO upwards to OT, placed 'above' IS. The girl is Miss Otis of Cole Porter's song Miss Otis Regrets, hinted by 'her regrets?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Otis, of the Cole Porter song Miss Otis Regrets, is the woman meant.

clue.text: Maybe Nigel, hot but loveless, can reduce weight

indicators.note: maybe signals a possible version of the letters, so they are rearranged
love is zero in tennis, the letter O, and loveless means that O is dropped

explanation.surface: A man named Nigel, ardent but unloved, can slim down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' drops the O (love, a zero score) from HOT, leaving HT; 'Maybe' rearranges NIGEL plus HT.
explanation.definitionFit: To lighten a load is to make it less heavy.

clue.text: Heraldic Loudmouth

parts.note: the Greek herald in the Iliad whose voice was as loud as fifty men's

explanation.surface: A noisy expert on coats of arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heraldic' suggests coats of arms, but means acting as a herald: in Homer's Iliad the herald of that name shouted as loud as fifty men.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud-voiced herald in Homer, whose name gives the adjective stentorian.

clue.text: Fairy dropped and died

parts.note: a peri is a fairy or sprite in Persian lore
to shed is to drop, as leaves or skin

explanation.surface: A sprite fell and passed away.
explanation.walkthrough: PERI is a Persian fairy, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To perish is to die, especially violently or untimely.

clue.text: Growing reserves

definitions.meaning: fragrant garden flowers, things that grow

explanation.surface: Increasing savings.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocks are sweet-scented garden plants, and also goods or supplies held in hand.
